public_rationale: Dario and Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic with other OpenAI alumni; Ilya Sutskever founded SSI; and Mira Murati founded Thinking Machines Lab. These are several prominent alumni across three rival AI organizations. The records support the ordinary career-transition reading. They do not establish a majority of departing leaders, identical private motives, or that all three organizations already sold competing products.
limitations: Competition includes advanced AI research and prospective products.
Schulman's move to an existing competitor is not counted as founding it.
The evidence establishes departures followed by founding; only the Anthropic interview directly discusses the group's reasons for leaving.

statement.excerpt: Many of those people left to start competitors.
statement.document_title: GPT-5: Overdue, overhyped and underwhelming. And that’s not the worst of it.

our_interpretation: “Those people” refers to prominent former OpenAI personnel, as in the preceding sentence.
The plain reading is that numerous prominent alumni departed and founded rival AI organizations. It does not mean that a majority of all departing leaders did so.
“Competitors” includes organizations pursuing overlapping advanced AI research and products, even if they had not yet shipped a direct ChatGPT substitute.
“To start” requires a documented connection between departure and founding. Joining an existing rival is insufficient.
The cumulative target period ends on August 9, 2025 and has no stated lower bound.
The phrase “many of” is a scope qualifier, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Records connect several prominent OpenAI alumni to founding rival AI organizations after leaving, with founding completed by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The alleged founders predominantly remained at OpenAI, only joined existing competitors, or founded organizations outside the relevant competitive field.
